from scipy import stats

answer_raw.explanation: The titer loss began right after a feed-water line fitting was replaced. The new fitting leaches metal ions into the culture, which poisons/aggregates product and raises broth turbidity. Evidence: at baseline titer was ~25 with turbidity ~41. Reducing feed-water flow to zero (exp4) restored titer to ~64 and dropped turbidity to ~5; adding a metal-chelating additive at 60 (exp5) independently restored titer to ~64 and dropped turbidity to ~6. Both interventions attack the same hidden metal cause. In contrast, the operators' leading theory of DO drift is a decoy: raising the DO setpoint to 80 (exp6) drove DO to 80 but left titer stuck at ~25 and turbidity at ~40 — DO correlates with titer only as a bystander, not a cause. Temperature was flat and uncorrelated. Turbidity is a genuine downstream marker of the metal-induced damage (it tracks the cause and falls when the cause is removed), while DO is a confounded bystander. Fix: chelate the leached metals and/or reduce feed-water ingress; long-term, replace/passivate the offending fitting.
